content: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday. Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric. To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy. “Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit. Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice). With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever. To meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside. Meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency. “That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event. In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found. To stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation. Many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build new sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall. “In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?” There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports. Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. chineseTitle: AI 数据中心再次扰乱混乱的联合国气候谈判
chineseSummary: 清洁能源革命取决于整个全球经济的电气化，正如耗电的数据中心正在激增一样。这是来自世界各地的代表在联合国气候变化大会（COP31）期间必须应对的挑战，该会议于周日在土耳其安塔利亚结束，气氛混乱且令人不满意。每年，与会者[...]
chineseContent: 清洁能源革命取决于整个全球经济的电气化，正如耗电的数据中心正在激增一样。这是来自世界各地的代表在联合国气候变化大会（COP31）期间必须应对的挑战，该会议于周日在土耳其安塔利亚结束，气氛混乱且令人不满意。每年，与会者都会努力兑现 2015 年巴黎气候协议中阻止气候变化的承诺。为了防止极端天气变得更加可怕，防止沿海社区遭受洪水，以及防止干旱破坏粮食和水系统，需要大幅削减温室气体排放。但为了用太阳能和风能而不是石油和天然气为家庭或汽车提供动力，它们需要采用电力。为此，今年谈判最令人期待的成果之一是达成协议，到 2035 年将电力在全球能源消耗中的份额提高到 35%，而目前这一比例约为 20%。然而，当数据中心导致电力需求猛增时，这就变得更难了。这使得新的人工智能数据中心的兴起成为一个气候问题，同时也引发了关于如何从化石燃料过渡到可再生能源的讨论。 “世界上每个气候部长都在考虑这个问题，并且在讨论中不可避免地会提到这个问题。这是更广泛的能源转型的一部分，”澳大利亚气候变化和能源部长、COP31气候谈判主席克里斯·鲍文(Chris Bowen)在COP31峰会开始时接受Politico采访时表示。尽管成为迄今为止时间最长的缔约方会议，辩论持续时间比原定时间长了两天，但官方谈判却严重破裂。代表们最终未能获得足够的支持来通过他们已经讨价还价了两周的“协议”。欧盟、英国和一些国家
